rationale: The only candidate (#15198) is a feature commit adding automatic requirements installation; it renames DESCRIPTION to description and moves requirements to a class attribute, which does not repair any defect in the description-fallback lines.
The candidate (#15208) is a variable-renaming commit that only joins the keyword-argument call onto one line and renames list_lightningapps to list_apps, with no behaviour change.

The fix for fake reauthentication narrows the pre-existing outer `except BraviaTVAuthError` so it covers only connect(); the blamed PSK/PIN connect branch was just re-indented into the new try block and did not cause the spurious reauth.

Despite its 'fix' prefix, the candidate extends the model-decorating codemod script (adds ALL_SILO_SPECIAL_CASES and an all_silo_model pass, drops the silo_limit filter); the blamed line was a correct rename to the newly public silo_limit attribute.

Candidate 1 adapts the call site to `.organization.slug` because a later service refactor changed the type of active_organization, and candidate 2 removes the onboarding client-state feature; neither repairs a defect in this refactor.

The fix for #31335 (removing Meta constraints/indexes on FKs on MySQL) repairs pre-existing logic; this preparatory 'Refs' commit only extracted _create_missing_fk_index and reformatted the _constraint_names call that the fix later replaced.
The candidate (#16346) is a refactor that moves CSVLogger logic into lightning_fabric and inherits from it; it removes the finalize() no-op guard as part of that restructuring, not to fix a defect.

This change is a pure rename, and both candidates are feature work (an OpenAPI retriever class with caching for CLI help, and printing plus sys.exit in place of exceptions) that carry the renamed lines along.

The new GraphQL blame query left the string arguments (name, owner, ref, path) unquoted, which is invalid GraphQL, and read `.get('blame', [])` even though the query itself nests results under `blame { ranges }`; the fix quotes the arguments and adds `.get('ranges', [])`.
The candidate ('hoists args out of else block') is a behaviour-preserving refactor that moves `args = None` ahead of the if/elif chain.

This change added `features.has('organizations:customer-domains', last_org)`, which can run with last_org=None; the follow-up adds a None guard, but its title says it was driven by stricter parameter validation in test patching, so it is unclear whether production behaviour was actually broken.

The fix adds tags[transaction] to the where-clause allow-list that this change created; its message blames not using the transformed transaction column (likely changed in other files), so it is unclear whether this change's restrictive allow-list or the new raise was itself the defect.
